compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

[rebar:2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9] adds an opt-in embedding retrieval tier whose vector build is an
explicit `build_vectors(tracker, *, limit=None)` in `src/rebar/similar/embedding.py`. That
design is deliberate: `find_similar` calls `catch_up` inline
(`src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:22`) and the create advisory calls `find_similar`
(`src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:196`), so anything catch-up does runs inside a user's
`rebar create`. A digest-and-embed pass there would put one LLM call plus one embed per ticket
on the create path.

The consequence is that nothing invokes `build_vectors` today. Until an operator calls it from
Python, every live entry is unvectored, coverage is never full, and `rank` returns `None` on
every call — the tier permanently degrades to lexical. The capability ships unreachable from
any supported surface.

## Decision: a `rebar store build-vectors` member

`rebar store` is already the storage-maintenance family — "Check, repair, measure, migrate, and
compact the ticket store" (`src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/store.py`), with members `fsck`,
`fsck-recover`, `doctor`, `maintenance`, `footprint`, `export`, `import`, `compact`
(`src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py:453-517`). Building the similar-ticket index is maintenance of
that same store, so the member belongs there.

Rejected: a new top-level `rebar similar` namespace. One command does not justify a new
top-level spelling, and `src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py` registers no `similar` route today.

Rejected: a periodic sweep hung off an existing path. `compact --all` sets the precedent that
the *command* is rebar's portable surface and the schedule is the operator's choice, made
outside rebar. A sweep that fires on its own would also have to decide when it is allowed to
spend provider budget, which is a policy rebar has no basis to set.

The family parser auto-enumerates `STORE_ROUTES` and pulls each member's help line from the
first line of that member's parser description (`advanced/store.py`, `_summary`), so adding
the route adds the member line to `rebar store --help` with no edit to the family parser.

## Design

1. **`src/rebar/similar/_cli.py`** (new) — `build_vectors_cli(argv)`. Precedent for a
   subsystem-local CLI module is `export`/`import`, whose handlers are `rebar._io._cli:export_cli`
   and `:import_cli` (`_registry.py:498`, `:506`).

   The handler resolves configuration itself before calling the build:

   - `embedding_model_name()` returns `None` → print a message naming `[llm] embedding_model`
     and **exit 0**. The build is never entered, so no provider is contacted.
   - otherwise call `build_vectors(tracker, limit=…)`. `status` `complete` or `partial` →
     exit 0. `status` `unavailable` → exit 1, message carries `reason`.

   Resolving "not configured" in the handler rather than string-matching `reason` is what keeps
   the two meanings of `unavailable` apart: an unconfigured install is a clean no-op, a provider
   denial is a failure the operator must see.

2. **`src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/similar_build.py`** (new) — `build(*, prog)`, modelled on
   `advanced/tracker_footprint.py`. Arguments: `--limit N` (cap the tickets vectored this run)
   and `--output {text,json}` (default `text`), matching `footprint`'s `--output` spelling.

3. **`src/rebar/_cli/_registry.py`** — a `Route("build-vectors", group="store", …)` appended to
   `_store_routes()` (`:444`), with `parser_factory="rebar._cli._parsers.advanced.similar_build:build"`,
   `handler="rebar.similar._cli:build_vectors_cli"`, `adapter="argv"`, `init="full"`. `init="full"`
   matches `maintenance` and `compact` (`:483`, `:516`): the build reads the index and the ticket
   event log, so it needs a mounted tracker.

4. **`src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/advanced/store.py`** — amend the family description to name the
   index build, since "check, repair, measure, migrate, and compact" does not cover it.

5. **Generated artifacts** — regenerate `src/rebar/_cli/help/store.txt` with
   `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py` and `docs/cli-reference.md` with
   `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py`. Both are drift-gated in CI.

6. **`tests/unit/test_similar_build_cli.py`** (new) — the ACs below.

## Portability

The surface added is a CLI command plus the already-public library entry point `build_vectors`.
Neither is tied to a CI system, and no capability here is reachable only through one. An install
with no provider configured runs the command to a clean exit 0 and keeps serving lexical
results, so the tier stays opt-in rather than becoming a dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar store build-vectors --help` exits 0 and its usage line reads `Usage: rebar store build-vectors`.
- [ ] `rebar store --help` lists `build-vectors` in the `commands` block.
- [ ] With no `[llm] embedding_model` set, the command exits 0, its output names `embedding_model`, and an embedding stub that raises on call is never invoked.
- [ ] With a stub embedding model configured over a tracker holding N live tickets, the command exits 0 and reports `vectored` = N; a second run reports `vectored` = 0.
- [ ] `--limit 1` over a corpus of 2 or more uncovered tickets exits 0 and reports `status` `partial` with `remaining` ≥ 1.
- [ ] `--output json` writes exactly one JSON object to stdout carrying `status` and all 5 counters from `_new_stats` (`vectored`, `skipped`, `empties`, `digest_unparsed`, `digest_failed`).
- [ ] An embedding provider that raises exits 1 and the message carries the failure reason.
- [ ] `rebar create` with an embedding stub that raises on call succeeds — the create path makes no provider call.
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_cli_help.py --check` exits 0 against the committed artifacts.
- [ ] `python scripts/gen_cli_reference.py --check` exits 0 against the committed artifacts.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full `make verify` pass.

## Testing

Every acceptance criterion above is proved by a named command, and each of the 12 maps
to one test in the new `tests/unit/test_similar_build_cli.py` unless noted:

- The `--help` criteria are proved by invoking the parser in-process and asserting on the
  captured usage text, so they need no subprocess.
- The counter, `--limit`, and `--output json` criteria run the command against a temporary
  tracker seeded with live ticket dirs and a stub embedding provider, so no network call is
  made and the assertions are on returned counters rather than on log text.
- The provider-raises criterion asserts the non-zero exit and that the reason survives into
  the message, rather than asserting an exact string.
- The `rebar create` criterion lives with the create-path tests, where the stub that raises
  on call is already the established fixture shape.
- The three generator criteria (`gen_cli_help.py --check`, `gen_cli_reference.py --check`,
  `check_mechanism_delta.py --check`) are repo-level gates run as commands, not as unit
  tests; `make lint` already invokes the mechanism-delta one.

Full proof before push is `make verify` from the implementation worktree, which is the
locally checkable half of CI's `Verified` vote.

## Out of scope

Scheduling the build (cron, launchd, a CI job) — the operator's choice, outside rebar.
Changing `rank`'s degrade contract or the create path's behaviour, both fixed by
[rebar:2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9].
